abstract: The melanocortin system is critical for energy homeostasis, yet our understanding of the circuits through which melanocortin signaling regulates thermogenesis remains incomplete. Here, we identify arcuate Kiss1 (Kiss1ARC) neurons as melanocortin-responsive regulators of brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis in male mice. Ablation of Kiss1ARC neurons induced obesity, while their chemogenetic activation increased BAT thermogenesis without affecting food intake. This increase in BAT thermogenesis is mediated by glutamatergic projections to dorsomedial hypothalamus (DMH) CART/Lepr neurons, which engage the raphe pallidus-BAT pathway. CRISPR-mediated Vglut2 deletion from Kiss1ARC neurons replicated the obesogenic effect. Deletion of the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene from Kiss1 neurons caused obesity due to increased energy balance. Optogenetic POMC fiber stimulation evoked MC4R-dependent inward currents in Kiss1 neurons. These findings reveal a melanocortin-responsive Kiss1ARC → DMH circuit that contributes to BAT thermogenesis, establishing Kiss1 neurons as components of the melanocortin pathway beyond their reproductive functions.
